title: Give the Mark III tap-shaped actions on the full table, and measure which rows a week reaches
tier_reason: Brain code behind the unit suite, the demo's gate and the replay round-trip; git reverts it. The table is ruled; the honesty of the measurement is the deliverable.
ask: WI-9b in docs/V0_2_1_PLAN.md: eight actions (till, plant, water, harvest, ship, shoo, wander, wait), each executed as her tap is — walk to the nearest legal tile in view, do the verb — with the router's legality; reward from the pre-state; plant and sell cues in farm.gd; the harness with crows, ripe crops and a seeded box; the gate restored to an assertion; a per-row report of what the linear learner reaches in a week.
source_message: CEO on Q-100, 2026-09-09, chief of staff session: the full reward table.
result: Landed on main (commit f2c1758 merged): eight tap-shaped actions with errand walking, reward from the pre-state, plant and sell cues (puff only, because her own are silent), the harness with crows, ripe crops and a seeded box, the gate restored as an assertion. Fixed seed: days 1-3 average 9.7 points, days 5-7 18.1; day 4 shipped a crop for 10. 24 farms, days 5-7, learning against control per row: shipped 5.56/0.97, harvested 0.58/0.10, watered_plant 7.81/6.11, planted 9.14/8.94, tilled 0.83/0.96, watered_soil 0.29/0.42, crows 0/0 on both rows. Gate: 8 farms 19.8 against 18.2, 6 of 8 rose; 24 farms 24.2 against 17.5, 20 of 24. LEARN_RATE 0.03 from a sweep (0.12 ends below the control). Unit 2425, integration 671, robot session and gateway green. Chief of staff verified on main after the merge.

follow_ups.title: Find out which farm jobs the learning robot never picks up
follow_ups.first_action: Run tools/demo_learning_robot.gd with per-choice logging of shoo, till and water_soil: record how often each is legal in view, how often it is chosen, and what reward it returns. Report whether the crow row is ever reachable at all versus never selected, and whether tilling and soil-watering are being crowded out by higher-reward verbs.
follow_ups.why: Crows are 0/0 on both rows and two rows end below control, so three of eight jobs are unexplained.

follow_ups.title: Give the robot's planting and selling the same sounds the player's actions have
follow_ups.first_action: Add plant and sell sounds for non-player actors and wire them to the cues in farm.gd, matching the loudness and timing of the player's own plant and sell sounds.
follow_ups.why: Her actions currently show a puff and stay silent, which breaks the rule that a watched actor gets the player's treatment.

follow_ups.title: Check how much room the learning-robot test has before an unrelated change turns it red
follow_ups.first_action: Re-run the learning assertion across ten different seeds at 8 and 24 farms and report the margin distribution, flagging whether any seed puts the learning average below the control.
follow_ups.why: The 8-farm assertion passes at 19.8 against 18.2 with only 6 of 8 farms rising, so an unrelated shift in the random stream could fail it without anything being broken.

recommend.question: Ship v0.2.1 with the Mark III learning six of the eight jobs, or hold it until she learns crows and tilling too?
recommend.answer: Ship the six and file the crow and tilling work as follow-up.
recommend.why: The learning result is already far above the control on the rows that matter, and the three missing rows are a diagnosis job, not a design change.
recommend.instead: Hold v0.2.1 until all eight rows rise, which buys a cleaner story at the cost of a release you can otherwise cut this week.
